source_snapshot.test_name_items: Hot plug/non hot plug FAN  exist  in BIOS/BMC log
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check Fan plug log in BIOS/BMC
1. Insert required fan on SUT
2. Power on
3. Go to UEFI setup menu to check power information
4. make sure system can boot without error
5. Check power module exist in BMC

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. No error during POST
2. Check fan rule in Spec
3. Check fan information in BMC

original_test_intent: Apparently verify that a fan insertion or presence condition, described ambiguously as hot-plug/non-hot-plug, is reflected in BIOS/BMC information or logs without POST error.
original_method: No safe executable method can be fixed from the source: the title implies live and/or cold fan events, while the numbered steps only insert a fan before power-on and then inspect unrelated power-information/module fields.
manual_activity: After unblocking, a qualified operator must perform the defined fan installation/removal at the approved power state and capture BIOS/UEFI evidence. No physical event should be attempted while the source scope is unresolved.
required_inputs: Decision whether the case covers live hot-plug, cold installation, non-hot-plug presence, or separate variants
Exact fan FRU/slot, platform hot-plug capability and electrical/ESD/power sequence
Expected BIOS/UEFI/BMC inventory or event/SEL fields and correlation timing
POST acceptance, cooling/thermal limits, final fan population and tested recovery
safety_requirements: Do not infer hot-plug support from the title or insert/remove a fan while powered without exact platform authorization.
Do not execute the cold-install sequence and claim hot-plug/event-log coverage.
Preserve baseline firmware/BMC/SEL/host evidence and require operator action timestamps after unblocking.
Stop on thermal, POST, connector, BMC or recovery anomaly; no repeated physical event or power cycle automatically.
agent_execution_scope: While blocked, retain source evidence and prepare only read-only inventory/log collection.
After a formal scope decision, collect complete BMC/SEL/host data and correlate it with operator firmware/physical evidence.
Do not claim the physical action or formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Resolve the event/power-state scope and power-versus-fan field wording.
Provide the approved module/slot procedure and execute/supervise the physical action after unblocking.
Define expected logs and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No command is proposed, appropriately, but its narrative invents a live hot-plug and post-event SEL workflow absent from the numbered source steps.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not recommend a command or physical sequence until the owner separates and defines the hot-plug and non-hot-plug variants. Later use full read-only BMC/SEL evidence only as support.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Title, cold insertion/power-on steps, firmware/BMC wording, criteria and both one-minute fields are preserved without reinterpretation.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create distinct owner-approved variants for cold-installed fan presence and live hot-plug event behavior, each with its own power procedure, expected firmware/BMC fields, event timing and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Unknown until fan module and hot-plug capability are identified.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record chassis/fan FRU, BIOS, BMC and CPLD versions after clarification.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform fan service/hot-swap and firmware inventory/event specifications are required.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Does not replace the source; proposes resolving its combined incompatible scopes into explicit variants.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents cold-presence evidence from being misreported as hot-plug coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Event scope, power state, fan map and log semantics.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A split is an engineering decision and cannot be applied to the master source by this review.

project_override_considerations: A project may explicitly approve one clarified variant and report only that coverage. Until then, neither a cold insertion nor a live action may be assumed to satisfy the library case.
expected_evidence: Engineering scope decision, platform hot-plug specification and fan/slot map
Approved physical/power sequence, event timing, firmware/BMC/SEL acceptance and recovery
After unblocking: physical action record plus POST/UEFI and complete BMC/SEL/host evidence
Restored fan population, thermal/boot health and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title combines hot-plug and non-hot-plug/log behavior, but the procedure only inserts a fan before power-on and defines no live removal/insertion event. It also asks for UEFI power information and a BMC power module while criteria require fan information. These are material method and target conflicts.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Necessary operation semantics—whether hardware is manipulated live or powered off, what event is generated, and what firmware/BMC field proves it—are unresolved. Guessing them creates electrical/cooling risk and invalid coverage.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keep its physical limitation but reject the invented live hot-plug/SEL interpretation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with BLOCKED and the requirement for owner scope, safety and event clarification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Documents both the event-scope and power-versus-fan conflicts so unblocking can be precise.

review_improvement: Prevents an unsafe live fan action and prevents a cold-presence boot check from being mislabeled as hot-plug validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: Hot-plug and non-hot-plug fan validation require different power states, hazards and evidence. Because the source never chooses one and its numbered fields appear copied from a power-module case, the operation cannot be safely or semantically inferred. This meets the narrow V3.1 BLOCKED threshold.
